name: teaser-detail-deeplink
display_name: Teaser list → full case, opened in place at a shareable URL
description: A list of teasers where activating one opens its full text in place — no page load — while the address bar gains a parameter that reproduces the same open state on a cold load. Rows with no full text are not offered as controls at all.

contract.outcome: the detail region becomes visible and is populated with THAT item's full body text (>200 chars of the item's own prose, not a class toggle on an empty node); the activated row is marked open
contract.address_effect: history.pushState adds ?<param>=<item key>; no navigation, no reload

contract.outcome: the detail region is hidden AND emptied (textContent cleared, not merely hidden); the open mark is removed; the address returns to the bare list URL
contract.why_emptied: innerText on a display:none element falls back to textContent, so a hidden-but-populated region still reads as content — an acceptance check can otherwise pass without the interaction having happened (sighted live 2026-07-26, gauntlet_dead_cta RUNBOOK §9)

contract.outcome: back/forward reproduces the open/closed state the URL names; the region never disagrees with the address bar

_SCHEMA_DELTA: Everything below this line is a field the draft DDL does NOT have. Each was forced by the live implementation, not invented — see HARVEST_01 §3.

entry_points.outcome: on first paint the named item's detail is already open, with no click — the URL is a real address for the state, not a decoration
entry_points.evidence: archive_loader_new.js currentSlug() + fillArchive() tail; live check B.2 (direct load)

requires_component_contract.why_not_restated_here: the openable/inert split is a RENDER-time property of the list, so it belongs to the component contract; a journey that restated it would create two accounts of one clause that drift apart (HARVEST_01 §3.6). The journey asserts only what activation DOES.

data_contract.shape: { <collection>: { entries: [ { key, date?, title, teaser, body?, url? } ] }, newest first
data_contract.absence_semantics: an entry without `body` is legitimate and MUST degrade to the non-openable state, never to a dead link
data_contract.cap: the loader renders at most N (vonc: 24) — a cap is part of the contract, not an implementation detail
data_contract.evidence: archive_loader_new.js data-contract header comment; provocations.json archive.entries[] (8 entries, 7 with detail_body, 1 without — the split is real live data, not a test fixture)

degraded_states.when: the feed is missing, non-200, or malformed
degraded_states.outcome: the list shell and its empty-state line are left exactly as built; nothing renders half-populated and no error UI is invented
must_not: render an openable row with no body
degraded_states.evidence: archive_loader_new.js fetch().catch() — graceful, documented in its header

item_template.note: the hidden row the loader clones

sample_item_key.note: bind-time: a key that is openable TODAY, so the criteria have something real to open

checks._unsupported: no check type asserts an EMPTY/absent state today; without it the innerText/display:none trap passes silently (HARVEST_01 §3.4)

checks._inherited: the anti-dead-control check (static rows carry no href/tabindex) is asserted by the required component contract feed-driven-teaser-list, not restated here
